changes: Fourth-batch source-reviewed publication. Cross-verified from official 0.5 patch notes, current creator guides, an independent build guide, a planner, a current gameplay video and community questions.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Hollow Palm Technique lets a Martial Artist fight with empty weapon slots: while both weapon sets are unarmed, your unarmed attacks gain a large amount of added damage and benefit from attack speed scaling. You start the campaign with a normal quarterstaff or wand and swap to unarmed once the technique and a basic defense layer are ready.

This is a verification-first guide. Exact APS, support links and unique thresholds are described from current creator guides; the swap timing, the unarmed rules and the Evasion-versus-Energy-Shield tradeoff are the actionable core.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Very fast clear once attack speed and unarmed scaling are online.
No weapon to upgrade means one fewer gear chase early.
Smooth league starter that scales into endgame.
Reuses Martial Artist tools (Bell, charges) for bosses.
cons: Unarmed requires both weapon sets empty - a real constraint, not a free bonus.
High attack speed raises mana, animation-lock and defense pressure; it is not automatically safer.
Copying a luxury high-APS version on a starter budget usually lowers damage.
Some bosses punish sustained melee uptime; rotate, do not face-tank.

sections.title: Is This Build Right For You?
paragraphs: Pick Hollow Palm if you want a fast unarmed Martial Artist and you are comfortable managing weapon-set swaps and a defensive layer before pushing attack speed. It is not a 'do-nothing' build: the speed only pays off once the foundation exists.
League starter and Hyper Speed are different budget tiers. Do not expect the creator's 18 APS showcase on a fresh character; build the starter first.

steps.label: Levels 1-23 - Weapon leveling
body: Level with a quarterstaff skill (e.g. a basic martial skill). Unarmed is not available yet; focus on survivability and attribute requirements.

steps.label: Levels 24-40 - Pre-Hollow setup
body: Reach the Martial Artist ascendancy and collect a basic Evasion/ES layer. Keep a weapon until Hollow Palm Technique and a defensive buffer are ready.

steps.label: Levels 41+ - Unarmed swap
body: Swap both weapon sets to unarmed once the technique is online. Add Tempest Bell and a charge source for boss tools.

steps.label: Waystones - Endgame
body: Push attack speed and added damage, then layer Energy Shield. Benchmark on T15 before chasing Hyper Speed rolls.

sections.title: Hollow Palm Transition Checklist
paragraphs: Unarmed is active only when every weapon slot in both sets is empty. Keep that rule in mind before removing a weapon 'for more damage'.
Transition only when: Hollow Palm Technique is available, a basic defense layer exists, and mana sustain is stable. Until then, keep leveling with a weapon.

sections.title: Unarmed and Defense Mechanics
paragraphs: Hollow Palm Technique reads your (empty) weapon slots and converts that into unarmed added damage. Facebreaker and the technique stack because both reward unarmed attacks; a normal gloved hand without the technique is just a hand.

Evasion and Energy Shield serve different jobs: Evasion reduces melee/bow hit chance, Energy Shield gives a recoverable pool that pairs with CI or hybrid. A high-APS character takes more hits per second, so defense must keep up - speed is not a substitute for it.

whyUse: Scales with attack speed and added unarmed damage.

recommendations: Facebreaker is the core unique; it rewards unarmed attacks with added damage. A rare glove with life/evasion is the starter alternative.
Prioritize Evasion/ES base. Hybrid bases are strong for the mixed defense plan.
Life, resistances, attribute requirements and a bit of attack speed. Do not over-invest before the core is stable.
Attack speed, added phys/cold, life. Luxury only after the core is solved.

steps.label: Starter -> Functional
body: Cap resistances, secure life/ES, equip Facebreaker.

steps.label: Functional -> Endgame
body: Raise attack speed and added damage; add Tempest Bell supports.

steps.label: Endgame -> Luxury
body: Chase Hyper Speed rolls and expensive jewels only after T15 is comfortable.

sections.title: Budget Variants
paragraphs: Starter uses a rare glove and a basic Evasion/ES layer. Functional Endgame adds Facebreaker and a Bell setup. Hyper Speed and Luxury are high-investment showcases - do not treat the creator's top APS as your default target.

sections.title: Defensive Layers
paragraphs: Evasion plus Wind Dancer/Ghost Dance is the baseline. Energy Shield (often with CI or a hybrid) adds a recoverable pool. Do not rely on attack speed alone - at high APS you take more hits per second, so the pool must be real.

sections.title: Mapping Rotation
paragraphs: For normal packs: establish the charge engine, then use your fast unarmed attack through safe lanes. Keep moving; the speed is the clear, not a tank stance.

sections.title: Rare Rotation
paragraphs: For rares: prepare charges and drop Tempest Bell before committing. Use a short defensive skill if the rare is dangerous; do not over-extend into a deadly modifier.

sections.title: Boss Rotation
paragraphs: For bosses: verify the charge and Bell sequence in the current client before treating the written order as final. Keep distance, use the Bell focus, and disengage on telegraphed slams - sustained melee uptime is not always safe.

sections.title: Bad Matchups
paragraphs: Bosses that punish sustained melee uptime or apply heavy degens are bad matchups. Rotate, use your defensive layer, and avoid face-tanking. Hollow Palm is not a 'all bosses are free' build.

sections.note: Short paraphrases of common community questions and concerns, edited for clarity. Not verbatim quotes.

items.question: When should I swap to Hollow Palm?
answer: Once Hollow Palm Technique is available, a basic defense layer exists, and mana sustain is stable. Before that, keep leveling with a weapon.

items.question: Does unarmed mean I need no gear?
answer: No. Unarmed only means empty weapon slots; you still need gloves (Facebreaker), armour, rings, amulet and a real defense pool. Empty weapon slots are a rule, not a free power.

items.question: Why does copying a high-APS version lower my damage?
answer: The showcase APS comes from expensive gear and specific rolls. On a starter budget you lack the supports and defenses that make the speed pay off, so damage and survival both drop.

items.question: Is high attack speed automatically safer?
answer: No. Higher APS means more hits taken per second. Your Evasion/Energy Shield must keep up; speed is not a defense substitute.

checks: Check that BOTH weapon sets have every weapon slot empty. A single equipped weapon disables Hollow Palm.
Reduce attack speed temporarily or add mana sustain/leech. The speed tax is real at high APS.
